text: In a directed graph with start vertex 1, vertex d dominates u if every path from 1 to u passes through d. Every reachable u ≠ 1 has an immediate dominator idom(u), the closest strict dominator, and the edges idom(u) → u form the dominator tree (支配树): d dominates u exactly when d is an ancestor of u in it.

Uses: "which single vertex removal cuts u off from the source" (灾难 P2597 on a food DAG), critical points in control-flow graphs. On a DAG, process vertices in topological order: idom(u) = LCA in the tree built so far of all u's predecessors. General graphs need Lengauer–Tarjan (below), O(m α(m)).

Lengauer–Tarjan: number vertices by DFS order. The semidominator sdom(w) = the smallest- numbered v from which a path reaches w using only vertices numbered above w in between. Compute sdom in reverse DFS order with a DSU-with-minimum ("eval"); then idom(w) = sdom(w) if the vertex with minimum sdom on the tree path sdom(w) → w is w itself, otherwise idom(w) = idom of that vertex.
A final pass in DFS order fixes the deferred ones.
